section_1.title: Prerequisite Refresher: The Mapping Concept
section_1.content: Briefly define a linear transformation as a mapping between vector spaces. Remind students that an m x n matrix represents a transformation from n-dimensional space to m-dimensional space.
section_1.example: Visualizing a 2D arrow (vector) being transformed by a matrix into a new position.

section_2.title: Expanding Dimensions (m > n): The 'Projection' Perspective
section_2.content: Explain how an m x n matrix (where m > n) embeds a lower-dimensional space into a higher-dimensional space. Visualize this as placing a 2D sheet of paper into 3D space.
section_2.example: A 2D character (a cat) moving inside a 3D room. The matrix maps the cat's local 2D coordinates onto specific 3D floor coordinates.

section_3.title: Compressing Dimensions (m < n): The 'Shadow' Perspective
section_3.content: Discuss dimensionality reduction. When m < n, the transformation 'squashes' information, effectively creating a projection or 'shadow' of the high-dimensional data.
section_3.example: Using a light source to cast the shadow of a 3D dinosaur figure onto a 2D flat wall. The matrix acts as the 'light' that simplifies the 3D data into 2D.

section_4.title: The Geometry of the Kernel and Image
section_4.content: Explain the concept of 'loss of information.' Emphasize that when compressing (m < n), multiple inputs can map to the same output, creating a 'kernel' (a null space) that represents the collapsed dimensions.
section_4.example: Several different 3D 'lego' structures casting the exact same 2D silhouette on a wall, demonstrating that the 3D depth information was lost in the transformation.

section_5.title: Synthesis & Real-world Application
section_5.content: Conclude by summarizing that non-square matrices are the engines of data processing—either expanding data for analysis (feature engineering) or compressing it for storage/visualization (PCA).
section_5.example: A robotic arm (device) with 3 sensors (3D) sending data to a controller that processes it into 2 motor commands (2D) to navigate a path.

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text("- " + line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (6x6 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 1.5 + j * 1.2
                y = 2.5 - i * 1.0
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Geometry of the Kernel and Image", 
                          ["Compression loses information permanently.", 
                           "Different inputs can yield the same output.", 
                           "This space of loss is the kernel."])
        
        # Objects
        # Kernel: A line
        kernel = Line(start=LEFT*1.5, end=RIGHT*1.5, color="#FF4500", stroke_width=6)
        # Image: A plane
        image = Polygon(UL, UR, DR, DL, color="#32CD32", fill_opacity=0.3, stroke_width=2)
        image.scale(0.8)
        
        # Positions
        self.place_at_grid(kernel, "C3")
        self.place_at_grid(image, "D4")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FF4500"))
        self.play(Create(kernel))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#32CD32"))
        self.play(Create(image))
